institutionName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To experience the American college life and school spirit with sportsgames, such as football and basketball, and a large variety of classes with the opportunity to explore something new

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: ConnectCarolina shows where your classes are and what classes you can swap to in the first week with available seats. The heellife website is good to see all upcoming campus events, for example for exchange students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was orientation with all the other exchange students and the study abroad advisor. She gave all the necessary information about our visas, important e-mail adresses to know, life in America etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Nicole Cobb (the study abroad advisor) and the rest of the team are so nice and welcoming. They can answer all of your questions

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It took some time to find off-campus housing via Facebook-groups but it was all worth it. If you are used to living on your own and like cooking your own meals, live off-campus with a kitchen and your own room. I lived at Lark and can recommend it (had my own room and bathroom)  

For Facebook groups, look at UNC Chapel Hill Subleases, Roommates, Off Campus Housing & Apartments and UNC Chapel Hill Housing and Sublease Community-North Carolina

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you can find a room in a house where someone is going on exchange themselves, that would be nice. Lark, Union Apartments and other furnished apartment buildings are in walking distance from campus and with nice amenities, like a gym and study spaces (some with a pool)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to take 400+ courses and not many classes left when I could register. But it is so nice that you can swap to other classes in the first week and visit them before you swap to see if you like them better

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registrered for 4 courses in April for fall 2023, but swapped 3 in the first week of classes. Easy to do in ConnectCarolina and KU quickly approved my new classes before I changed

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: ConnectCarolina is easy to navigate and the study abroad advisor sends a guide on how to sign up for classes. She is also helpful with responding to e-mails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful with registration, but I got a seat in the classes I wanted to swap to in the first week

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the nice opportunity and visit some other classes in the first week if you are not quite happy with one or more of your classes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was nice to be able to have classes both in the humanities and social sciences because I needed electives for 30 ECTS (12 credits)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to take 400+ courses as an MA student enrolled as a senior at UNC (BA-level)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of them were similar with Powerpoint lectures and class discussions, but more group work in my sociology class than I am used to at UCPH. Oral history and performance was very different with class discussions in a circle and class exercises

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LING 541- Sociolinguistics
COMM 562- Oral History and Performance
SOCI 433- Immigration in Contemporary America
PWAD/COMM 574- War and Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can highly recommend SOCI 433 with Emma Labovitz. She is so engaging with the material and with the students

It was fun to try something more creative in COMM 562 with a public performance as the exam, where we in groups had interviewed a former director of an institute on campus

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Former residents in my apartment had taken some things with them, so my roommates and I had to buy cheap plates and cutlery in Target

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries in the supermarkets were more expensive than expected

Very nice that the busses in Chapel Hill/Carrboro are free

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many options for clubs and sports. Intramural sports, Carolina Outing Club and whatever interests you may have

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Carolina Outing Club is great for exchange students. 20 dollars for a semester and you can sign up for all their events, like hikes, bouldering gym, campfires and camping. They take care of transport and they are so nice and welcoming

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to all the sportsgames you can, even if you are not that much into sports, to experience the school spirit. Football, basketball, soccer, field hockey, volleyball etc.

Explore Chapel Hill and Carrboro as well other places in North Carolina. I can recommend the Blue Ridge Parkway in the fall and Asheville. Washington DC is so nice as well

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Relatively easy. So much fun to experience the school spirit at sportsgames. The Southern cuisine is very different, but nice to try

Chapel Hill is such a nice small campus town and everyone wears UNC merchandise to show school spirit

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to events or try a club to meet Americans. I met many nice Americans for example at a block party, Random Acts of Kindness club and Carolina Outing Club

Talk to people in class. It was my experience that they were very interested to hear more about Denmark

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The heat and humidity in August and September were a lot to go through, but a cap is great to have with you during the day

The air condition in the class rooms, libraries and in my apartment building was challenging to get used to with the contrast of humid summer weather

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: School spirit, school sports and the small campus town was so fun to experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the opportunity to visit other classes in the first week

Sportsgames are free, but for football and basketball, you have to sign up for the lottery

Explore events and clubs on the Heellife website

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I could only sign up for a year lease at Lark apartments, but managed to find a subleaser for the other half of the year. So it is an option if you are looking for off-campus housing

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience American campus life with other exchange students and Americans

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The heat and the humidity in August and September

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Explore the local places, like Carolina Coffee Shop, He´s Not Here, Top of the Hil, Supdogs, Que Chula, Roots etc.

Visit places out of state if you have the time. Washington DC and New York are relatively close to North Carolina

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
